newsitem.title: UK: Dixons sees 10 mln stg warranty tax hit.
newsitem.headline: Dixons sees 10 mln stg warranty tax hit.

text.p: British electricals retailer Dixons Group Plc said the impact of tax changes on warranties sold with its products would be less than 10 million stg.

Dixons has found a way of reducing the impact of last year's hike in insurance premium tax levied on the sale of extended warranties, sold alongside its products. By introducing new service contracts which are liable for VAT, but not the insurance tax, Dixons is able to reclaim some of the VAT.

Chief executive John Clare said, "We think the hit to us as a group as a result of the tax changes will now be somewhere...under 10 million, rather than the gross hit which would have been much more than that."
Clare told Reuters in an interview that prices of warranties and service contracts have had to go up overall by about six or seven percent as a result of the tax changes.
He said although it was early days the group was quite encouraged by the sales performance.
"We are seeing some sales elasticity to the price increases but not as much as we might have feared."

He said Dixons' Mastercare extended warranty business represented between eight and nine percent of sales and at a net product level the policies made about the same for the company as selling a television or a hifi.
Clare saw little impact on the electricals market if the government decides to act on recommendations from the Monopolies and Mergers Commission to ban manufacturers' recommended retail prices.
Press reports in May suggested the MMC would seek to scrap the recommended prices, but the Department of Trade and Industry has yet to announce its decision.
Clare said if recommended prices were banned it would have no impact on Dixons. But if there were to be a price war the losers would likely be the smaller independents, he said.
